summary: Full-stack test of Mediq waitlist feature + sapphire/emerald theme + fonts + dark mode. Backend: 9/9 pytest passed (POST /api/waitlist creates entry with id/email/position/already_registered=false; duplicate -> already_registered=true; case-insensitive dedup; invalid email -> 422; invalid role -> 422; default role works; GET /api/waitlist/count returns count + display_count where display_count == count + 12400; count increments after create). Frontend: every required data-testid present (hero-waitlist-email/submit/role/role-ug/role-pg/role-other, final-waitlist-email/submit, plus all 30+ legacy testids). Hero submit with valid email shows success pill 'You're in - spot #N. We'll email you when your slot opens.' Final-CTA submission also returns success pill (testid final-waitlist-success). Caption updates from '12,407+ medics ahead of you' to '12,409+ medics ahead of you' after two real submissions, proving GET /count integration. Theme: h1 fontFamily='Outfit, Manrope, sans-serif', body='Manrope, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif' (NOT Roboto). Light primary button bg = rgb(15,82,186) (#0F52BA sapphire). Dark mode body bg = rgb(5,8,20) (#050814) with primary btn rgb(59,130,246) (#3B82F6). Zero white-section leaks in dark mode. No console/page errors. Invalid-email Snackbar verified with 'abc@def' -> 'Please enter a valid email address.'.
critical_code_review_comments: WaitlistForm relies on browser-native HTML5 type=email validation as a first line; for truly malformed inputs (e.g. 'not-an-email') the browser tooltip fires and React Snackbar never shows. The custom regex Snackbar only fires for emails that pass HTML5 but fail the stricter regex (e.g. 'abc@def'). Both behaviours block submission, but if the spec mandates the Snackbar always appear, add noValidate to the form so the React handler always runs.
WaitlistResponse exposes incremental position which can leak total signup count to anyone POSTing; consider returning only a bucketed/encrypted position for production.
GET /api/waitlist/count is unauthenticated and could be scraped to enumerate growth; rate-limit if abuse is a concern.
Frontend axios import is fine but project already has fetch elsewhere - consider standardising on one HTTP client to reduce bundle.

MongoDB collection 'waitlist' has no unique index on email; current dedup is application-level via find_one. Race condition possible under high concurrency. Add `db.waitlist.create_index('email', unique=True)` on startup.
EmailStr requires email-validator package (which appears installed since 422 returned) but requirements.txt should explicitly pin it to avoid silent breakage on rebuild.
test_credentials: N/A - waitlist is public, no auth required
seed_data_creation: Test entries created in MongoDB 'waitlist' collection prefixed with TEST_ (emails like TEST_create_<ts>@example.com, TEST_ui_<ts>@example.com). Not cleaned up automatically - main agent may purge with: db.waitlist.delete_many({email: {$regex: '^test_'}}) if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mediq waitlist endpoints live at <REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL>/api/waitlist (POST) and /api/waitlist/count (GET). Pydantic EmailStr enforces RFC email validation (returns 422). Duplicate dedup is case-insensitive and matches by lowercased email. display_count = count + 12400 (warm baseline). Frontend: WaitlistForm component used by Hero (testIdPrefix='hero-waitlist') and FinalCTA (testIdPrefix='final-waitlist', dark=true). MUI TextField wraps the actual input - selector pattern: page.locator('[data-testid="hero-waitlist-email"] input').fill(...). Success state replaces the form with a pill (data-testid='<prefix>-success'). Theme uses palette mode + localStorage 'mediq-theme'; sapphire #0F52BA light / #3B82F6 dark, emerald #10B981, body fonts Outfit (headings) + Manrope (body).
